final_message:
I've built the three-tab workbook, and both schedules match the GL balances you gave to the cent for January through April 2025 (variance $0 every month). I recalculated the workbook with an independent formula engine because Excel isn't installed here, and every check came out at zero. The last rebuild only changed one note's wording.

| | Prepaid Expenses (1250) | Prepaid Insurance (1251) | Total |
|---|---|---|---|
| Invoices | 41 | 25 | 66 |
| Year-to-date prepaid additions | $1,087,156.21 | $568,698.22 | $1,655,854.43 |
| Year-to-date amortization | $527,778.60 | $198,721.52 | $726,500.12 |
| **Ending balance 4/30/2025** | **$559,377.61** | **$369,976.70** | **$929,354.31** |

**What's in each tab**
- **Prepaid Summary:** a header with "Aurisic" and the 1/1/2025–4/30/2025 period, then the snapshot above. Below that are a month-by-month roll-forward against the GL, year-to-date amortization by expense account, and a notes and assumptions section. Every figure is linked to the two detail tabs.
- **Prepaid Expenses (1250) and Prepaid Insurance (1251):** one row per invoice, sorted by vendor, with subtotals for vendors that have more than one invoice. Each row shows the original amount, the amortization start and end dates, number of months, monthly expense, the monthly amortization and the remaining balance each month. At the bottom of each tab are:
  - a monthly activity summary (beginning balance, additions, amortization, ending balance), checked against the invoice detail and the GL;
  - the monthly amortization split by expense account, which you can post as the monthly journal entry.

**How I treated the invoices**
- **Service periods:** none of the prepaid-services invoices states a period, so all are spread over 6 months starting in the invoice month. This default is what makes the schedule match the GL in every month.
- **Good Insurance:** spread over 12 months (1/1/2025–12/31/2025).
- **BCBS:** each monthly payment covers the following month. So the 1/1/2025 invoice, due 1/15, is expensed in February. That leaves one month of coverage in 1251 at each month-end, which matches the GL.
- **Rounding:** monthly expense is calculated at full precision and displayed in cents. Rounding each invoice's monthly expense to cents would leave the schedules a few cents off the GL by April ($0.01 on 1250, $0.05 on 1251).

**Assumptions you may want to confirm** (all are listed in the Summary notes; none of them changes the 1250 or 1251 balances)
- "Subscription" invoices go to 6762 Subscription Fees/Service Agreements; 5220 Software Subscriptions is the alternative if they are software licenses.
- The UHY "Advising" invoices go to 5720 Consulting Fees, since the chart of accounts has no exact match.
- Good Insurance goes to 5400 Insurance - Comm/Prop/Liab/Other, because the invoices don't say what type of coverage they are.
- "ADOBE MAGENTO" (January) and "Magento" (April) have different addresses, so I kept them as separate vendors.
- The months after April on the detail tabs only carry forward invoices already received; they don't include future invoices.

The `workspace/` and `attachments/` folders mentioned in the instructions weren't in the folder, so everything comes from `reference_files/`. The build script is `scripts/build.py`.
